So im not sure if you guys know about the informal relationship between Imgur and Reddit which became a formal business investment relationship and the danger it poses but my real concern is that this startup, which is basically a startup with the exact same relationship that imgur and reddit had will some day become a professional relationship with real investments and shared interests to protect. A little tl;dr is that imgur was started by a Redditor which wanted an easy to use image hosting site for reddit users to put pictures on it without any restrictions. After a few years of side by side development, the two sites realized their shared goals and interests and began to make a official partnership. Then subreddits started to implement rules like all images have to be hosted on imgur or you get deleted and silly shit like that. The Reddit users started to believe this rule as being for the benefit for the website because, in all honesty, the Imgur platform was really clean and easy to use. They started to flame and downvote people who didnt use imgur with comments like "wtf, why isnt this on imgur, why are you using photobucket its such a trashy site" and what not.

Then eventually Reddit and Imgur started to protect each others interests when Reddit went on to ban /r/fatpeoplehate because FPH was making fun of and mocking the Imgur employees. Obviously as a partner in business, you cant tolerate one site from degrading the other and ruining any professional relationship that had been built and so came the ban hammer.

So anyways, what Im trying to get at here is that I would really really really hate it for Veuwer and Voat to go down the same path as Imgur and Reddit to where they are willing to put their business relationship before the users of the site. While I appreciate what the creator/owner of Veuwer is doing for the Voat community, I see the parallels between that and Reddit/Imgur which leads down a very dark path. Ive seen some people already calling Veuwer,the "official Voat image hoster" which rings alarm bells for me because that is the same exact line that people used for Imgur/Reddit.

Anyways, I hope you guys share my concern and have a plan to avoid the downfall that we saw with Imgur/Reddit.
